newsitem.title: USA: Raytheon sells home appliance, air conditioning and commercial cooking businesses.
newsitem.headline: Raytheon sells home appliance, air conditioning and commercial cooking businesses.

text.p: Raytheon Co. said Monday it agreed to sell its home appliance, heating and air conditioning and commercial cooking businesses for $750 million, transferring the Amana and Caloric home appliance brands to Goodman Holding Co.
The sale price includes $550 million in cash and $200 million from the sale of Raytheon Appliance Group receivables.

With the appliance units sale, Raytheon leaves the business that created the company in 1922. Founded as the American Appliance Co. with plans to make refrigerators, the company switched instead to radio tubes, invented the microwave oven and later became the nation's largest missile maker and a major weapons contractor.

Earlier this month, Raytheon bought the defence electronics business of Texas Instruments Inc. for $2.95 billion. Lexington, Mass.-based Raytheon is awaiting government approval of its $9.5 billion merger with Hughes Aircraft, announced in January.

Raytheon said it will retain its commercial laundry business, which makes Speed Queen coin-operated washers, as well as the electronic controls segment of the Raytheon Appliance Group. However, the high-technology company said it is continuing its strategic assessment of these two businesses.
In 1996 the two business segments combined accounted for about 20 percent of revenues and 50 percent of profits for the Raytheon Appliance Group, it said.
Raytheon said the sale is expected to be completed in the third quarter, subject to U.S. government approval.
Goodman, a privately held company based in Houston, owns several businesses, including Goodman Manufacturing Co., a major participant in the heating and air conditioning business.

Raytheon bought Amana Refrigeration in 1965 from the Amana Society, which was founded by a religious sect, and got a first-rate consumer appliance company that could market the microwave oven that Raytheon invented at the end of World War Two.
The first Raytheon microwave ovens, named Radarange by the company's employees, were sold to restaurants and hospitals during the 1950s for about $3,000.

Raytheon, based in Lexington, Mass., also bought two other appliance makers, Caloric and Speed Queen. Caloric made Glenwood and Sunray appliances, while Speed Queen makes the Marathon line of washers and dryers.
Raytheon's stock added 62.5 cents to $54.8125 on the New York Stock Exchange.
